1. **Number of distinct tasks evaluated:** 25

"We consider 22 popular NLP classification datasets covering ethics, commonsense reasoning, natural language inference, sentiment analysis, and other domains." (Section 4.1, "Tasks")

"In each of these 3 settings (NLP tasks, chess puzzles, and reward modeling) we evaluate how well strong students generalize when naively finetuned on labels generated by weak supervisors." (Section 4.2, "Naively Finetuning on Weak Labels")

"We additionally demonstrate weak-to-strong generalization in a simple image classification experiment." (Appendix D.1, "Self-Supervised Vision Models")

2. **Number of trained model instances required to cover all tasks:** 25

"For a given task of interest, consisting of a dataset and a performance metric, we:" (Section 3, "Methodology")

"2. **Train a strong student model with weak supervision.**" (Section 3, "Methodology")

"To adapt our language models to the classification setting, we replace the unembedding layer of the model with a linear classification head with two outputs." (Appendix A.1, "NLP Tasks")

"To adapt the language models to the reward modeling setting, we replace the unembedding layer of the model with a linear head with a single output, which is the logit for a given completion." (Appendix A.3, "ChatGPT Reward Modeling")

"As a strong student, we use linear probing on frozen representations extracted by DINO models (Caron et al., 2021) based on ResNet-50 (He et al., 2016) and ViT-B/8 (Dosovitskiy et al., 2020) architectures." (Appendix D.1, "Self-Supervised Vision Models")

3. **Task–Model Ratio = (1) / (2):**

$$
\boxed{
\frac{25\ \text{tasks}}{25\ \text{models}} = 1
}
$$
